source.title: Toward Faithful Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Sparse Autoencoders
source.authors: Guang-Zhi Xiong; Zheng-Hao He; Bo-Han Liu; Sanchit Sinha; Ai-Dong Zhang

record.tranche_reason: The study examines SAE-derived features in LLMs and their semantic consistency, and qualifies strong interpretations of SAE features by noting that some may remain generic or polysemantic. It does not test toy-model superposition geometry.
record.gate_note: Detection performance with RAGLens and the feature-level analyses are the study's own results. Comparisons to other detectors are not recorded here. Layer-wise trends, feature-count sweeps, and predictor comparisons are mostly shown in figures and concern detector design rather than superposition geometry. The feature-explanation prompts and mitigation prompts are instructions to models used in experiments, not instructions addressed to an AI reading or reviewing the paper.
record.test_reason: The paper is a RAG hallucination detector (RAGLens). It treats pretrained or self-trained SAEs as a feature extractor and reports its own detector's performance (Table 1, Fig. 2–5, Tables 2, 5, 9). The feature-interpretation case studies (Table 3, App. E, H, I) and causal interventions (App. C) serve to show that the detector's selected features are interpretable. They do not test whether LLMs store features in superposition, whether SAE features are complete, stable or canonical units, or whether features are 1-D. Detection AUC is method performance, not evidence on any version. The polysemanticity caveat in App. E is a cited, unquantified acknowledgement of prior work.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that SAE features from LLM internals give accurate, interpretable RAG hallucination detection (RAGLens beats baselines), with mid-layer, high-MI features and GAMs working best. They report that explanations enable effective feedback-based mitigation, and that causal intervention on features works in some cases but is not universal. The note that some SAE features may be generic or polysemantic is a brief caveat citing prior work, not a finding.
record.recipe_differences: The original source studies toy networks and geometric superposition; this paper uses pretrained or separately trained SAEs to probe LLM activations for RAG-hallucination detection and mitigation. It does not reproduce the original method.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported detector performance varies by dataset, task, model, and layer; layer trends also differ by task, with a comparatively flat pattern for Data2txt. These analyses concern detection performance, not superposition geometry.

fits_no_version.finding: With MI selection and a GAM, SAE features keep detection performance at small K' better than raw Llama2-7B hidden-state dimensions, especially on AggreFact and TofuEval; the two are comparable at large K' (App. D, Fig. 6).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE dictionaries concentrate task-relevant (hallucination) signal into fewer dimensions than the raw neuron or hidden-state basis.

fits_no_version.finding: Clamping SAE feature 22790 (Llama3.1-8B) to +20 steers outputs away from unsupported numbers, and clamping to -20 or 0 does not. Features that fire only on hallucinated tokens cannot be used preventively (App. C, Tables 6–7).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Detector-selected SAE features can causally steer generation in some cases; this is a steering effect with no behaviour rate.

record.problems: The direct feature-interpretation and counterfactual evidence is qualitative and based on selected examples; the GPT-5 explanation check covers 24 cases for one feature. The authors do not test completeness or canonicality, and they acknowledge that some SAE features may be generic or polysemantic. Several analyses are presented as plots without exact values in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant rows omitted. Detector comparisons against other methods, feature-count and layer sweeps, and mitigation results were not included because they measure detector design or induced mitigation outcomes rather than the representational claims in the listed versions.

untested.parts: No toy models, geometry or sparsity transition.
No capacity or importance analysis of neuron polysemanticity.
No measurement of how features spread across neurons; SAE recoverability is assumed rather than tested.
No completeness, stability across seeds or sizes, or canonicality tests; only selected-feature interpretability anecdotes.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T5' rests on treating detector AUC and selected-feature anecdotes as evidence for V4/V5. The paper assumes SAE monosemanticity as a premise and never tests it, so all rows are unlinked and no verdicts are given.

versions.untested_parts: No toy networks, feature-over-dimension setup, overlap geometry, sparsity transition, or regular geometric arrangement is tested.
No test of neuron polysemanticity as a consequence of competition for limited representational capacity, or of important features receiving dedicated dimensions.
No test of causes of polysemantic neurons independent of capacity pressure.

The study tests whether SAE features from real LLMs carry RAG-hallucination signals useful for detection. It does not measure how features are distributed across neurons or establish general feature recovery beyond this task.

The study examines semantic interpretations and context sensitivity for selected features, but does not establish that SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units across models, datasets, or training conditions.
The study treats SAE features as scalar coordinates but does not test whether the represented features are intrinsically one-dimensional rather than multidimensional.

rows.subject: Llama3.1-8B
rows.operation_detail: GPT-5 rated expected activation from a natural-language feature explanation, compared with actual SAE activation.
rows.measure: Pearson correlation between GPT-5 predicted activation scores and actual SAE activations
rows.note: The paper describes the explanation as reliably capturing activation patterns, but this test covers one feature and does not establish completeness, stability, or canonical status of SAE features.
rows.check: Explanation-to-activation correlation (0.6731) for one detector-selected feature. It is an auto-interpretability check of a selected feature and does not test completeness, stability or canonicality (V5) or feature spread (V4).

rows.subject: Llama3.1-8B
rows.operation_detail: Examined top-activated cases to assess the interpretation of feature 22790 on the pretraining corpus.
rows.measure: Qualitative consistency of high-activation examples with the feature interpretation
rows.value: The authors report consistent activation in scenarios where responses are about to produce specific numbers or dates likely to be hallucinated.
rows.note: This is a qualitative analysis of selected high-activation cases, not a test of completeness or stability across conditions.
rows.check: Qualitative top-activation inspection of one selected feature on lmsys-chat; it does not measure any version's property.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Llama2-7B and Llama2-13B on RAGTruth and Dolly
reader_labels.reason: RAGLens using SAE features reports AUC values of 0.8413, 0.8764, 0.8964, and 0.8568, with accompanying accuracy and F1 results, showing that SAE-derived signals in these LLMs predict RAG hallucination labels (r1-r12).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Selected Llama3.1-8B feature 37877 in RAGTruth counterfactual case studies
reader_labels.reason: The feature's activation responds to whether numeric content is supported by the edited context, and falls when the context is removed in the QA case (r15-r20).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Selected feature 22790 and feature 37877 case studies; the paper's general discussion of SAE features
reader_labels.reason: Some individual features show interpretable and context-sensitive patterns, but the tests cover selected cases and do not establish complete, stable, canonical units; the authors also acknowledge generic or polysemantic features (r13-r21).
